To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the reaction of 1,3‐dithianes with lithium amides and hexamethylphosphorous triamide (HMPT) in tetrahydrofuran (THF) at room temperature yields 1,3,4‐thiadienes in high yields.

the activation of ketones by the Lewis acid hexamethyldisiloxane (HMDS) is an efficient method for the preparation of ketimines and that the subsequent reaction of these ketimines with lithium amides and hexamethylphosphorus triamide (HMPA) leads to the synthesis of a wide variety of haloketones and 1,4-diketones.

(a) the reaction of LiNR _{2} with HMPA leads to a new reagent, which is a powerful base and nucleophile and which can be used for the synthesis of a wide range of compounds, and (b) this reagent can be used for a variety of transformations of ketimines and imines.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the synthesis of new compounds and the development of new synthetic methods.
the development of new methods for the preparation of ketones and 1,4-diketones.
the synthesis of ketimines by the condensation of amines with ketones, their metallization by activated amides, and the subsequent alkylation or acylation of the resulting metalloketimines.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the reaction between an amine and an alkyl halide is not a nucleophilic substitution reaction.
the reaction of the ketimine with the amide is a nucleophilic substitution reaction at the carbon of the ketimino group.
the reaction is not catalysed by the metal, but by the amide.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

we have shown that the chemistry of ketimines can be extended in several ways: (a) The ketimine chemistry can be extended to include the preparation of ketimine derivatives of the type R1R2N=C(OR3)X (X = O, S, NR1, PR2) which are stable compounds.

we have shown the first example of a catalytic asymmetric reaction of a ketone with a nucleophile, and we have shown the potential of a new catalyst for the synthesis of a variety of biologically important compounds.
we are able to prepare 1,4-diketones from ketiminium salts in good yield.
The main takeaway from our work is that
we can use the metal–ligand cooperative effect (MLCE) to activate a C(sp 3 )–N bond, and this is an unprecedented example of the activation of a C(sp 2 )–N bond.
the use of a metal catalyst is not required for the formation of the C–C bond in the coupling reactions.
the reaction of ketones with lithium amides is not a simple matter of nucleophilic addition to the carbonyl group, but rather the reaction of the enolate anion with the amide.
